prompt:
This email, given as numbered sentences, is a company's reply to a person who asked it to delete their data. Most such replies only confirm they received it: then answer "wait". Answer something else only if the email clearly tells the person to do one thing now:
"scheduled" - it says the account is already scheduled to be deleted.
"no_account" - it says no account was found for the person's email address.
"verify_link" - click a verification link or enter a code.
"go_ahead" - reply YES, I AGREE or similar to confirm they may delete.
"confirm_sender" - write again from the account's own email address, or it says it cannot accept requests from third-party services.
"clarify" - say what should be deleted.
"provide_info" - send more details.
"use_form" - fill in a privacy or request form.
"log_in_delete" - sign in and delete the account themselves.
Mentions of a help center, a ticket number or logging in to view the case do not count. Give the number of the one sentence that shows the answer.

wait.headline: {company} has your request
wait.why: Nothing to do yet. They have until 1970-02-01 under EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

scheduled.headline: {company} will delete the account
scheduled.why: Do not sign in before then: signing in cancels the deletion.

action.label: Nothing to do. Stay signed out.

no_account.headline: {company} found no account under {email}
no_account.why: Then there is nothing of yours to delete under this address. If you signed up with a different email, send the request again from that one.

verify_link.headline: {company} sent a link or code to check it is you
verify_link.why: This is a fair check, done through your own email. Click it before it runs out, or the request closes.

action.label: Open the email and use the code or link in it

go_ahead.headline: {company} is ready to delete and wants a written yes
go_ahead.why: Reply YES and they go ahead. Their warning that it is permanent is what you asked for.

action.label: Write the reply
action.subject: Re: {subject} [{ref}]

confirm_sender.headline: {company} wants to know the request really comes from you
confirm_sender.why: It does: it was sent from {email}. One short reply from this address answers it.
legal: Article 12(2) GDPR requires you to facilitate the exercise of my rights, and the EDPB's Guidelines 01/2022 confirm a request may be sent to a controller's official contact point instead of its preferred channel. I sent it to your privacy address.

action.label: Write the reply
action.subject: Re: {subject} [{ref}]
action.body:
Hello,

This request comes from {email}, the email address on my {company} account, and I sent it myself from this address. It was not sent by a third-party service.
Please go ahead and erase my {company} account and all personal data you hold about me.
Article 12(2) GDPR requires you to facilitate the exercise of my rights, and the EDPB's Guidelines 01/2022 confirm a request may be sent to a controller's official contact point instead of its preferred channel. I sent it to your privacy address.

Reference: {ref}

Kind regards,
{name}

clarify.headline: {company} asks what you want deleted
clarify.why: Answer: everything. One reply settles it.

action.label: Write the reply
action.subject: Re: {subject} [{ref}]

provide_info.headline: {company} asks for more details
provide_info.why: Give only what links you to the account: your name and the account email. Nothing more is needed to find it.
